item.title: Indiana leaders have mixed reactions to operation "Epic Fury" in Iran
item.description: Leaders from Indiana are reacting to Saturday’s airstrikes in Iran.

item.title: Wife of Indiana congressman Jim Baird dies after car crash injuries
item.description: Danise Baird, wife of Indiana congressman Jim Baird, dies after complications with car crash injuries.

item.title: Are microschools a solution to falling public school enrollment? One Indiana district thinks so
item.description: A rural Indiana school district leader started a network of microschools to help keep students in his schools. The model could spread.

item.title: IPS adopts new student policy in latest move involving ICE lawsuit from Attorney General Rokita
item.description: The Indianapolis Public Schools board adopted a new policy on student privacy Wednesday in response to a lawsuit from the state attorney general claiming the district unlawfully impeded federal immigration enforcement.

item.title: How will a war in Iran affect Hoosiers?
item.description: Hoosiers should expect gas prices to go up as fighting in the Persian Gulf continues.

item.title: AES Indiana's parent company to go private in BlackRock-led $33B buy; Democrats decry
item.description: AES, the parent company of AES Indiana, announced on Monday that it has agreed to be purchased for more than $33 billion by a group of large domestic and foreign investors — and could go private as soon as this year.

item.title: At a pivotal moment for data centers, Indiana lawmakers take little action
item.description: As data center development continues across Indiana — drawing economic praise but growing concern over energy and land use — lawmakers advanced little legislation in the 2026 session to regulate the tech sector.

item.title: Lugar Plaza is now a park. That means it's easier to make arrests
item.description: You aren’t allowed to smoke, drink or use ‘abusive language’ at Indy parks.

item.title: ACLU of Indiana sues Ball State over protest rules
item.description: The plaintiffs are students who have protested against Ball State, mainly asking it to divest from any financial ties to Israel. The ACLU says university policies violated their First and Fourteenth Amendment rights.

item.title: Gov. Mike Braun gives himself 'B+' on 2026 session, calls Trump's Iran action 'long overdue'
item.description: Indiana Gov. Mike Braun is giving this year’s legislative session a “B+,” saying 51 of his 58 priority bills passed.
